stories.title: Spike: Rails on the snapshot, and a request-spec harness on a clone
stories.description: Prove that this app boots and serves its current pages against the local snapshot, and leave behind the test harness every later story uses. Delivers: the local run recipe (`config/database.yml` already reads every database name from the environment and has test entries, so it is not edited); a script that makes test clones of the snapshot databases (`CREATE DATABASE … TEMPLATE`) and remakes them on demand; RSpec with a helper of our own that never touches the schema; a guarded development task that creates clearly fake test accounts in a clone; one request spec against an existing page. Records the gate command in `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/config.yaml`. Out of scope: Vite, Inertia, any new page, any migration.
acceptanceCriteria: With the app running against the snapshot, GET `/`, `/resources`, one `/resources/{type}` and one `/resources/{type}/{id}` return 200. Evidence: the curl status lines in the handoff.
`bundle exec rspec` runs a request spec for the old `/resources` page against a clone and passes. Evidence: the rspec output in the handoff.
After the spec run, `ar_internal_metadata.environment` on the snapshot database is unchanged and `git diff db/schema.rb` is empty. Evidence: the query result and the diff output.
The clone script, run twice, ends with fresh clones and exit code 0, and refuses to run when its target name equals a snapshot database name. Evidence: both runs' output.

The fake-accounts task creates one normal user and one admin whose emails end in `@example.test`, and exits non-zero in production or when the connected database is not a clone. Evidence: a spec for the guard and the task output.

The Gemfile test group is byte-identical to the one on `origin/qiraat/p0-3-rspec-setup`, and `.rspec` matches that branch. Evidence: `git diff origin/qiraat/p0-3-rspec-setup -- .rspec` is empty and the Gemfile hunk is quoted.

The spike answers are recorded in the handoff: Ruby and Node versions used, required environment variables, what does and does not work without Redis, and the gate command, which is also written to `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/config.yaml`.

The planning facts that the 24 later commits on main could have changed are re-checked, and each one that is now wrong is corrected in `lessons.md`. Evidence: the list of facts checked and the entries added.
stories.notes: Read lessons.md Planning Context and the private sprint notes (team drop) first: they hold the snapshot connection details and the data-safety rules. If `qul-next` or the sprint branch does not exist locally, create `qul-next` from main and the sprint branch from `qul-next`; never push `main`. Do not name the helper `spec/rails_helper.rb`: the qiraat branch adds that file and it calls `maintain_test_schema!`. In test, `QulQuranRecord` connects to the `qul_quran_content_db_test` entry and the CMS side to the `test` entry; both read `QUL_*_TEST_DB_*` variables (defaults `qul_quran_content_test` and `qul_cms_content_test`). dotenv does not load in test, so the helper or a wrapper script must supply those variables when the clones have other names. `tests.yml` CI loads every `test/**/*_test.rb` without bundler: put nothing that boots Rails under `test/`. qiraat edits `database.yml` against the file's old layout; this story should not need to edit the file at all. `/docs/` is gitignored at the repo root. Main moved 24 commits after planning (see lessons.md, top). `config/database.yml`, the content-record class name, the issue forms and the workflows were re-checked at `3d805f64` and the notes corrected. Before anything else, re-check the remaining planning facts about `config/routes.rb`, `db/schema.rb` and `bin/setup` against the current tree and record what changed in lessons.md. The local `main` branch can be behind `origin/main`: compare against `origin/main` or the merge base, never local `main`.

done: App served against development clones of the snapshot (`bin/rails server`, Ruby 3.3.10): `200 GET /`, `200 GET /resources`, `200 GET /resources/surah-info`, `200 GET /resources/surah-info/3`, `200 GET /resources/translation` (curl status lines). No Redis was running; the log has no Redis errors.

`bin/snapshot-clones [test|development]` drops and remakes `qul_cms_content_{test,dev}` and `qul_quran_content_{test,dev}` with `CREATE DATABASE … TEMPLATE` from `qul_cms`/`qul_quran` (overridable with `QUL_SNAPSHOT_CMS_DB_NAME`/`QUL_SNAPSHOT_QURAN_DB_NAME`), marks each with `COMMENT ON DATABASE … 'qul snapshot clone of <source>'`, then applies the 7 CMS migrations the snapshot lacks through `migration_context.migrate` (no schema dump). Run 1 and run 2 each printed both `fresh copy` lines and `applied 7 pending CMS migrations`, exit 0. With `QUL_CMS_CONTENT_TEST_DB_NAME=qul_cms` it printed `Refusing: qul_cms is a snapshot database name.` exit 1; same for `qul_quran`.

RSpec: `bundle exec rspec` → `5 examples, 0 failures` (`Resources catalog (old page) lists the published resource types`: GET /resources is 200 and links /resources/translation; plus 4 FakeAccounts examples).

Snapshot untouched: `select value from ar_internal_metadata where key='environment'` on `qul_cms` → `production` after the spec runs; `git diff --exit-code db/schema.rb` → no diff. The snapshot databases have no comment; the clones carry the marker.

`spec/clone_helper.rb` (not `rails_helper.rb`) boots Rails in test, loads `.env.test.local` with Dotenv, never touches the schema, aborts in `before(:suite)` unless both connections are marked clones, sets transactional fixtures and `host! 'localhost'` for request specs.

`bin/rails dev:fake_accounts` (lib/fake_accounts.rb, lib/tasks/fake_accounts.rake): run twice on the dev clone → `reader@example.test (normal_user)` and `admin@example.test (admin)`, exit 0, idempotent (psql shows exactly those two rows, role 0 and 2). On the snapshot (`QUL_CMS_CONTENT_DB_NAME=qul_cms`) → `qul_cms is not a snapshot clone (see bin/snapshot-clones).` exit 1. In production → `Fake accounts are never created in production.` exit 1. Specs cover both guards. Jobs go to the :test adapter and deliveries are off inside the task.

Gemfile test group byte-identical to `origin/qiraat/p0-3-rspec-setup` (hunk: `group :test do` / `  gem 'rspec-rails', '~> 7.1'` / `end`, appended after `view_component`). Gemfile.lock hunks identical to that branch's (rspec-core 3.13.6, -expectations 3.13.5, -mocks 3.13.8, -rails 7.1.1, -support 3.13.7). `git diff origin/qiraat/p0-3-rspec-setup -- .rspec spec/spec_helper.rb` is empty (both copied from that branch).

Gate: `bin/gate` (standalone `test/` suite without bundler, then `bundle exec rspec`), recorded as `checkpoint_cmd` in `.agents/config.yaml`, in AGENTS.md and in the constitution's Quality gate. `package_test_cmd` is now `bundle exec rspec {files}`. AGENTS.md added to `rule_docs`.

Spike answers (also in AGENTS.md): Ruby 3.3.10 (Docker's version; host had none in range), Node 24.19.0 on the host for `yarn install`/`yarn build`/`yarn build:css`. Env: `QUL_{CMS,QURAN}_CONTENT_DB_{PORT,PASSWORD}` (+HOST when not localhost) in `.env`, the `_TEST_` equivalents in `.env.test.local` (both gitignored), `CDN_HOST=https://static-cdn.tarteel.ai`; names stay at defaults. Without Redis: all pages serve; anything that enqueues a job fails (sign-up welcome email, resource update mail, API client registration, admin todo mail); `Sidekiq.redis(&:ping)` → `RedisClient::CannotConnectError`. Rails needs a JS runtime (ExecJS) to boot.

Planning facts re-checked (routes.rb, schema.rb, bin/setup, SQLite exports) and added to lessons.md as two entries: route-helper names now taken by contributor routes, the snapshot is 7 migrations behind main (dev raises PendingMigrationError without them), bin/setup unchanged in substance, SQLite export table replacement; plus test-env and boot traps (hosts.rb in test, dotenv require order, ExecJS, escompress/esbuild, lockfile platforms).
decisions: Development also runs on clones (`bin/snapshot-clones development`), not on the snapshot. The snapshot is 7 migrations behind main and development raises PendingMigrationError on every page; migrating the snapshot would rewrite its `production` metadata guard. The AC's 'running against the snapshot' is met by an exact copy of it.
Clones are told apart by a database comment rather than by name, so the fake-accounts guard and the spec helper check a positive marker that the snapshot can never carry by accident.
Migrations on clones run via `ApplicationRecord.connection_pool.migration_context.migrate`, which does not dump `db/schema.rb` (db:migrate in test would).
Pinned the rspec gems in Gemfile.lock to the qiraat branch's exact versions (bundler resolved newer patches) so merging that stack later has no lockfile conflict.

The test connection lives in a gitignored `.env.test.local`, loaded explicitly by `spec/clone_helper.rb` and `bin/snapshot-clones` (`dotenv` is a development-group gem but `Bundler.setup` exposes all groups). The Gemfile's other groups are unchanged.

This machine's host toolchain was wedged during the run (clang, ps and top hung; load average ~350), so Ruby 3.3.10 could not be compiled on the host. All Ruby commands ran in a `ruby:3.3.10-bookworm` container (`qul-dev`, gems in volume `qul-dev-bundle`, snapshot via host.docker.internal:5433); AGENTS.md documents that path as 'Running in Docker instead'. The container is stopped, not removed: `docker start qul-dev`.
The fake account password is a fixed constant in lib/fake_accounts.rb: the accounts exist only in local clones, and later Playwright stories need a known login.
concerns: RuboCop could not run: the repo's `.rubocop.yml` requires `rubocop-minitest`, which is not in the bundle (pre-existing). New Ruby files were not linted.

Inside the Linux container, host `node_modules` binaries (esbuild) cannot run: escompress logs esbuild errors while rendering (pages still 200) and the first rspec boot printed one esbuild error. On a host Ruby this does not happen. Tailwind in the container needs the aarch64-linux platform gem installed in the container only.

The host-run recipe in AGENTS.md (Ruby on the host, localhost:5433) was not exercised end to end on this machine because of the wedged toolchain; only the Docker path was. `brew install ruby-build` was left installed on the host.
Each `bin/snapshot-clones development` run wipes local dev data, including fake accounts; rerun `bin/rails dev:fake_accounts` after it.
`bin/gate` itself was not run end to end (builders do not run checkpoint_cmd); its two halves were: rspec green, and `bash -n bin/gate`. The standalone `test/` half needs a host Ruby without bundler.

stories.title: Spike: Inertia, Vite, React and SSR beside the existing pipeline, with generated types
stories.description: Install the new front-end stack so it coexists with Sprockets, esbuild, the Tailwind 3 gem and Turbo, and settle every open integration question before pages are built. The result stays: `vite_rails`, `inertia_rails` (Inertia v3 client, React 19, TypeScript), Tailwind 4 through the Vite plugin, a source tree in `app/frontend`, an Inertia-only layout and base controller, SSR in development, Alba plus Typelizer for prop types and typed route helpers with a drift check, Vitest, ESLint and Prettier for the new tree, and one sample page behind a development-only route. Extends the gate command with typecheck, lint, component tests and the drift check. Out of scope: the production image (001-03), real pages, the UI kit.
acceptanceCriteria: The sample Inertia page returns HTML that contains its server-rendered text in development, and hydrates without a console error. Evidence: a request spec with `render_component` and `have_props`, and a `browser-verify` check of the console.

Every existing layout still loads its assets: `/`, `/resources`, `/tools`, `/users/sign_in` and one `tool` layout page render with no missing-asset request. Evidence: `browser-verify` network check on each, and `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) -- app/views/layouts/application.html.erb app/javascript esbuild.config.js config/tailwind.config.js` is empty.
`yarn build` and `yarn build:css` produce the same file list in `app/assets/builds` as on the merge base with `origin/main`. Evidence: the two listings.
Changing a serializer attribute without regenerating makes the drift check exit non-zero; regenerating makes it pass. Evidence: both outputs.
A typed route helper generated from `config/routes.rb` is used by the sample page's link. Evidence: the generated file path and `tsc` output.

Recorded answers, each with the evidence that settled it: (a) Tailwind 3 gem and Tailwind 4 npm do not affect each other's output; (b) a Turbo Drive link from an old page to the Inertia page, and a plain link back, both load correctly; (c) Devise sign-in from the Inertia page returns to it, and sign-out from it works when the target is an old page; (d) CSRF works with `protect_from_forgery with: :exception` and `xsrf_cookie_refresh: :lazy`; (e) server-managed meta tags can carry title, canonical, Open Graph and a JSON-LD script, with and without SSR; (f) redirects to this host are not turned into external redirects behind the proxy headers nginx sets; (g) Typelizer can or cannot generate without a database connection, which decides whether generated files are committed; (h) `alba-inertia` works or does not with the installed versions for typed page props including deferred props; (i) Inertia's client has a built-in helper for a plain same-origin JSON request, or `fetch` is used.
A component test runs under Vitest and a deliberate SSR hazard (reading `window` during render) is caught by a lint rule or an SSR render test. Evidence: the failing and passing outputs.
stories.notes: Set `sourceCodeDir` to `app/frontend` in `config/vite.json` BEFORE running any installer: `vite install` picks `app/javascript` when it exists, which is esbuild's tree. Both the Inertia generator and `vite install` inject tags into `application.html.erb` and may replace `bin/dev` and `Procfile.dev`; revert those and put the tags in the Inertia layout. Keep the package.json `build` script for esbuild (jsbundling runs it); use `ssrBuildEnabled` for the SSR build, not a changed `build` script. Inertia v3 needs the `use_script_element_for_initial_page`, `use_data_inertia_head_attribute` and `always_include_errors_hash` options and `config.version = ViteRuby.digest`. Vite and its plugins go in `dependencies`, test and lint tools in `devDependencies` (see 001-03 for why). Keep yarn classic and `yarn.lock`; do not touch `bun.lock`. The Inertia layout must not load Turbo; consider `turbo-visit-control: reload` in it. Under foreman the js process gets its own PORT; add the Vite dev server to `Procfile.dev` without changing the existing lines. Only `notice` and `alert` flash keys reach the client by default. Check version-sensitive facts against the installed packages or current docs, not memory. RuboCop's config requires a plugin that is not in the Gemfile: do not make RuboCop part of the gate unless it runs clean on new files with a scoped config. If (h) fails, the fallback is hand-written page prop types plus `have_exact_props` request specs.

done: Stack installed without running any installer. Gems: vite_rails 3.11.1, inertia_rails 3.23.0, alba 4.0.3, alba-inertia 0.1.4, typelizer 0.14.0. The Gemfile.lock diff only adds these gems and their deps; no platform was added. npm, pinned exact: vite 8.3.5, vite-plugin-ruby 5.2.6, @inertiajs/react and @inertiajs/vite 3.9.1, react and react-dom 19.3.1, @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.2, tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/vite 4.3.3 as dependencies; typescript 6.0.3, vitest 5.0.5, jsdom 30.1.3, @testing-library/react 16.3.3, eslint 9.39.5 (was ^8.55), typescript-eslint 8.72.0, eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1, @types/react* 19.3.0, globals 17.13.0 as devDependencies. Yarn classic; bun.lock untouched.

Files: config/vite.json (sourceCodeDir app/frontend, dev port 3036 → public/vite-dev, test 3037 → public/vite-test, production ssrBuildEnabled, ssrEntrypoint ~/entrypoints/inertia.tsx), vite.config.mts (RubyPlugin, @inertiajs/vite with the SSR entry, react, tailwindcss), app/frontend/{entrypoints/inertia.tsx, styles/inertia.css, pages/dev/InertiaSample.tsx, types/, routes/, test/}, layout app/views/layouts/inertia.html.erb (no Turbo, turbo-visit-control reload, inertia_meta_tags + inertia_ssr_head), InertiaController (alba-inertia controller, layout inertia, shared props from SharedPropsResource), Dev::InertiaSamplesController (show/create/ping) under `if Rails.env.local?` at /__dev/inertia_sample, ApplicationResource (Alba + Typelizer::DSL + alba-inertia helper, lower_camel keys), config/initializers/inertia_rails.rb (version ViteRuby.digest, always_include_errors_hash, use_script_element_for_initial_page, use_data_inertia_head_attribute, server_head, xsrf_cookie_refresh :lazy, ssr_enabled in development only), config/initializers/typelizer.rb, bin/vite binstub, `vite: bin/vite dev` appended to Procfile.dev.

AC1 SSR: in development, curl /__dev/inertia_sample → 200 and the HTML has `<div data-server-rendered="true" id="app">` with the <h1> and paragraph text, and the meta tags in the SSR head. Browser (agent-browser, real Rails): the page hydrated (React keys on #app), the deferred count showed 'Published resources: 547', and `errors` printed nothing. Request spec spec/requests/dev/inertia_sample_spec.rb uses render_component('dev/InertiaSample'), have_props(heading:, signedIn: false), have_deferred_props(:publishedResourceCount) and inertia_load_deferred_props. Full suite: `bundle exec rspec` → 16 examples, 0 failures.

AC2 old layouts: in the browser, /, /resources, /tools, /users/sign_in and /compare-font (tool layout) loaded every same-origin resource with status 200, and no Vite request was made. The guard `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) -- app/views/layouts/application.html.erb app/javascript esbuild.config.js config/tailwind.config.js` printed 0 lines.

AC3 builds: app/assets/builds was cleared and rebuilt before and after the change (yarn build, the six sass build:css:* scripts, then Tailwind 3 through the container's binary). Both runs gave the same 23-file list. tailwind.css is byte-identical (sha 6e11d455…). application.js and active_admin.js differ only in one esbuild path comment: tslib 2.8.1 moved from node_modules/tslib to node_modules/@swc/helpers/node_modules/tslib, and `cmp` shows the file contents are the same.

AC4 drift: `bin/rails typelizer:check` (lib/tasks/typelizer_check.rake) regenerates into temp dirs and compares the full file set. Adding a `subheading` attribute to Dev::InertiaSamplesShowResource without regenerating → 'Generated TypeScript is stale … app/frontend/types/serializers/DevInertiaSamplesShow.ts', exit 1. After `bin/rails typelizer:generate` → 'up to date', exit 0. The attribute was then reverted and the files regenerated.

AC5 typed route: the link 'Go to the home page' uses `root().url` from app/frontend/routes/index.ts, generated by Typelizer from config/routes.rb. The sign-in, sign-out, form-post and ping URLs are also route helpers. `yarn typecheck` (tsc -p app/frontend/tsconfig.json) exits 0.

AC6: Vitest runs app/frontend/pages/dev/InertiaSample.test.tsx (jsdom, 3 tests) and InertiaSample.ssr.test.tsx (node, renderPageOnServer runs createInertiaApp's server render function, as the SSR bundle does): 4 passed. With `const currentPath = window.location.pathname` added to the render, the SSR test failed with `ReferenceError: window is not defined` (vitest exit 1). With the page restored, 4 passed.

Spike answers (also in the AGENTS.md section 'Inertia pages'). (a) Tailwind 3's tailwind.css is byte-identical, and Tailwind 4 output (@import 'tailwindcss' source('../'), app/frontend only) has no font-title, font-sarina or font-inter. (b) A Turbo Drive link injected into /resources (Turbo session drive=true) loaded /__dev/inertia_sample as a full document: the old page's window marker was gone, window.Turbo was undefined and the page hydrated. The plain <a> back loaded / with Turbo present. (c) Browser: Sign in → /users/sign_in?user_return_to=%2F__dev%2Finertia_sample → reader@example.test returned to the sample page, showing 'Sign out'. Sign out (plain form post with _method=delete and the token from the meta tag) → POST /users/sign_out → / (old page) showing 'Login'. Both are also in request specs. (d) Spec with forgery protection on: an Inertia POST without a token → 422; with the XSRF-TOKEN cookie sent as X-XSRF-TOKEN → redirect plus flash notice. A second GET sent no new XSRF-TOKEN Set-Cookie (lazy). Browser: 'Send a test form' POST → flash 'The form was received.' (e) Server-managed `meta:` (title, description, canonical, og:*, ld+json script) is in the HTML without SSR (request spec, test env) and with SSR (dev curl). (f) An Inertia POST with Host qul.tarteel.ai and X-Forwarded-For only → 302 to http://qul.tarteel.ai/__dev/inertia_sample, with no X-Inertia-Location. A full https URL on an http request → 409 X-Inertia-Location (middleware spec). (g) Generation without a database (DB hosts pointed at db.invalid; a runner connect fails): explicit `typelize` serializers and route helpers generate. A `typelize_from DownloadableResource` serializer aborts with ActiveRecord::DatabaseConnectionError, and with the database it yields number/string/boolean. So the generated files are committed. (h) alba-inertia works: `inertia: :defer` gives a deferred prop (spec), and Typelizer types it optional (`publishedResourceCount?: number`). (i) Yes: `useHttp` from @inertiajs/react. Browser 'Ask for JSON' → XHR GET /__dev/inertia_sample/ping 200 with the URL unchanged. Core's http client sends X-XSRF-TOKEN on same-origin requests.

Gate: bin/gate now runs the standalone tests, `bin/rails typelizer:check`, `yarn -s typecheck`, `yarn -s lint:frontend`, `yarn -s format:frontend`, `bundle exec rspec` and `yarn -s test:frontend`. Each new step exited 0 when run separately; bin/gate itself was not run (driver-owned). .agents/config.yaml: package_typecheck_cmd 'yarn -s typecheck'. AGENTS.md documents the commands, the integration answers and the Docker recipe (Vite on the host, socat in the container).

Review fix: Rakefile sets VITE_RUBY_SKIP_ASSETS_PRECOMPILE_INSTALL=true before load_tasks. Without it, vite_ruby's assets:precompile hook would run a second `yarn install` with NODE_ENV=development in the Docker build, installing devDependencies (Cypress, Puppeteer). Verified: after load_rakefile, ENV is 'true' and assets:precompile has 2 actions.

Prettier is scoped to the new files through .prettierrc.json overrides only (old files keep the defaults). .prettierignore skips the generated dirs. eslint.config.mjs (flat) covers app/frontend and the Vite configs.
decisions: Rails ran in the stopped `qul-dev` container (host Ruby is 2.6), and Vite ran on the host (node_modules holds macOS binaries). Rails reached the dev server through `socat` inside the container (localhost:3036 → host.docker.internal:3036), so vite_ruby's proxy and the inertia SSR POST use Host localhost:3036, which Vite's host check allows. No Vite allowedHosts hack is in the committed config. Request specs use a host-built public/vite-test plus VITE_RUBY_AUTO_BUILD=false in the container. On a host Ruby, autoBuild works as configured.

Vite configs are vite.config.mts and vitest.config.mts. package.json has no "type": "module" (esbuild.config.js uses require), and a .ts config was bundled as CJS, failing on ESM-only @inertiajs/vite. tsconfig lives in app/frontend/tsconfig.json, not the root: esbuild looks for a tsconfig.json upward from app/javascript files and would pick up a root one.

Kept the existing global yarn `resolutions`. They force picomatch 2.3.2 on vite, vitest and tinyglobby, minimatch 3.1.5 on typescript-estree, and postcss 8.5.28 on vite. Path-scoped resolutions either were not applied or crashed yarn 1.22 ('should have a resolved reference'). Vite build, SSR build, Vitest, tsc and ESLint all work with the forced versions. typescript-estree only uses minimatch for allowDefaultProject, which this config does not use.

Dropped eslint-plugin-ssr-friendly: 1.3.0 crashes on ESLint 9 (context.getScope). The AC's SSR hazard check is the SSR render test pattern (*.ssr.test.tsx with renderPageOnServer). Every later page should get one.

Shared props and the ping JSON come from SharedPropsResource, so their TS type (SharedProps) is generated, not hand-written. Only FlashData (notice/alert, matching inertia_rails' default flash_keys) is hand-typed in app/frontend/types/inertia.d.ts.

Typelizer route helpers are generated only for included routes (config/initializers/typelizer.rb: /__dev/*, /users/sign_in|sign_out, /). Later stories add their routes to `routes.include`. Generating all of them would produce hundreds of files.

The sample routes live under `if Rails.env.local?` (development and test), so request specs can reach them and production has none. alba-inertia names the page serializer by convention: Dev::InertiaSamplesShowResource for Dev::InertiaSamplesController#show.

Sign-out from Inertia pages is a plain HTML form post, not router.delete. Devise redirects to an old (non-Inertia) page, which an Inertia XHR cannot show. The CSRF token is read from the layout's meta tag in the submit handler, so it is SSR-safe. No change was made to Devise controllers.

eslint 8 → 9 in devDependencies, needed for flat config and typescript-eslint. The old `yarn lint` script (app/javascript) had no config before and still does not lint anything; it was already broken.
concerns: Production image not exercised (story 001-03). vite_ruby now adds `vite build` and `vite build --ssr` (ssrBuildEnabled) to assets:precompile. The Dockerfile runs precompile twice and installs Node 24, which Vite 8 needs (≥20.19). A host SSR build succeeded (public/vite-ssr/ssr.mjs, createServer on 13714). The image build itself was not run.

inertia_rails includes its controller concern into ActionController::Base. Every old HTML page now sets a non-HttpOnly XSRF-TOKEN cookie on a visitor's first response, and again when invalid (lazy policy); spec probe on /resources confirmed it. The gem has no per-controller opt-out. This matters if any HTML caching layer bypasses on Set-Cookie. It is documented in AGENTS.md.

inertia_rails also adds `etag { inertia_conditional_get_variant }` and `Vary: X-Inertia` handling to all controllers. Old pages rendered and loaded their assets normally in the checks above, but conditional-GET behaviour on old pages was not specifically tested.

On 4 of the 5 old pages, the browser showed a 403 from https://api.github.com/repos/TarteelAI/quranic-universal-library: an anonymous GitHub API call from existing page JS, not an asset. Not compared against the merge base.

RuboCop could not lint the new Ruby files. The repo config needs rubocop-minitest (missing), and the bundled RuboCop 1.31 crashed even on a scratch config. This was already broken. `ruby -c` passed on all new Ruby files.

In development, with ssr_enabled and no Vite dev server, each Inertia request tries localhost:13714, fails fast and falls back to client rendering with a Rails.error report. bin/dev starts Vite, so this only happens when Vite is not running.

No committed browser-test harness exists yet (no browser_verify keys in .agents/config.yaml). Browser checks were interactive agent-browser runs against real Rails (development clone, Vite on the host), and no Playwright spec was left behind. Story 001-05 adds the harness.
The qul-dev container now has socat installed (apt). It was left stopped, as 001-01 left it.

stories.title: Spike: production image build and SSR service under Passenger
stories.description: Prove the production Docker image builds with the Vite client and SSR bundles and serves server-rendered pages, with Node running as one more runit service beside Passenger, and that pages fall back to client rendering when that service is down. Delivers the Dockerfile, service and nginx changes, the SSR settings (URL, a short timeout, error reporting), and a local recipe to build and run the image safely. If SSR under Passenger cannot be made reliable, deliver the fallback from PRD spike S3 and record why.

stories.title: Spike: glyph-per-page mushaf rendering and one font URL rule
stories.description: Answer whether a mushaf page of the three glyph-per-page layouts (QPC V1, V2, V4 Tajweed) can be rendered in React from the page's word rows with one font per page from the CDN, server-rendered and SSR-safe, and fast enough with the indexes the content database has today. Also settle the single rule that maps a font, script or layout resource to its font files, replacing the two existing builders that disagree. Delivers a throwaway-quality page on the development-only route, the query, the font URL resolver with tests, timing numbers, and a recommendation that 001-15 builds on. Unicode layouts are checked for one Madani and one IndoPak layout so the line model covers both.
acceptanceCriteria: Pages 1, 2, 300 and 604 of QPC V1, V2 and V4 Tajweed render with the same line breaks and glyphs as the old preview. Evidence: side-by-side screenshots of the old and the spike page for each, saved outside the repo and described in the handoff.
The page query time (cold and warm) for one glyph layout and for the 1890-page 9-line layout is recorded, with the query plan. Evidence: the numbers and `EXPLAIN` summary in the handoff.

The font URL resolver returns a URL that answers 200 for every published font resource and for the per-page fonts of the three glyph layouts, or lists the resources for which no working URL exists. Evidence: a named test for the rule and a one-off sweep output.
Centered lines, surah-name lines and bismillah lines are placed from the line-alignment rows for one Madani and one IndoPak unicode layout. Evidence: screenshots of a surah-opening page for each.
The handoff states pass or fail against PRD spike S4 and, on failure, which fallback 001-15 must use for which layout.
stories.notes: Facts are in lessons.md (layout and font sections). Known traps: one content row can map to two mushafs and the existing lookup has no order; one mushaf has more page rows than its page count (clamp); one published layout has no word rows; one layout has almost no bismillah alignment rows; the V4 Tajweed font has no font-face entry so the old builder makes a broken URL; one font's value has a typo. The two databases are separate: no SQL join between line alignments (CMS) and words (content). The content database is never changed, so no new index. `CDN_HOST` must be set locally. Load only the font for the page shown; never preload 604 fonts.

done: S4 verdict: PASS. QPC V1 (layout 15), V2 (layout 10) and V4 Tajweed (layout 19) pages render in React from mushaf_words with one font file per page from the CDN, server-rendered (curl of /__dev/mushaf_pages/10?page=2 has data-server-rendered and the @font-face rules in the HTML), and the page query needs no new index. 001-15 builds on this; no fallback is needed for these three layouts.

Spike page: GET /__dev/mushaf_pages/:id?page=N (Dev::MushafPagesController, inside the existing `Rails.env.local? || QUL_INERTIA_SAMPLE_PAGE` routes block), :id is a published mushaf-layout DownloadableResource id. Page component app/frontend/pages/dev/MushafPage.tsx renders lines from props, inlines @font-face for the page font only (plus the surah-name, surah-header and bismillah fonts only when the page has such lines), and the V4 light font palette. Props: Dev::MushafPagesShowResource with MushafLayouts::LineResource, MushafLayouts::WordResource, FontFilesResource, FontSourceResource; generated types DevMushafPagesShow, MushafLayoutsLine, MushafLayoutsWord, FontFiles, FontSource and route helper devMushafPage.

Line model: app/services/mushaf_layouts/page.rb. MushafLayouts::Page.mushaf_for(resource) takes the content row's `mushaf` meta key, else the enabled mushaf with the lowest id for the content row. Page.new(mushaf, n) clamps n to 1..pages_count (Mushaf Qatar has 610 page rows for 604 pages; ?page=610 → 604, ?page=0 or abc → 1). #lines loads words (content DB) and line alignments (CMS DB) in two queries and returns the lines that have words or an alignment row, each as {number, centered, surahNumber (null unless a surah-name line), bismillah, words[{id, text, charTypeName, verseId}]}. Surah name and bismillah are separate flags because the 16-line IndoPak layout (mushaf 7) has rows that are both (layout 11 page 187 line 3, surah 10).

AC1 (same line breaks and glyphs): pages 1, 2, 300, 604 of layouts 10 (V2), 15 (V1), 19 (V4 Tajweed): a headless-Chrome DOM comparison of the old preview (/resources/mushaf-layout/:id?page=N) and the spike page found the same lines, line kinds and glyph sequence on all 12 pages (compare_all.txt) (e.g. 10/p300: 15 lines, 140 words each), no line wrapped to a second row in either, and the page font loaded (document.fonts: v2-p300 etc.). Side-by-side screenshots (old left, new right) saved outside the repo in the builder's scratchpad (shots/side-<layout>-p<page>.png); zoomed V4 p604 line shows identical glyphs and tajweed colours. Differences are cosmetic only: vertical spacing around surah headers and bismillah.

AC2 timing (development clone; EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) of the exact query `WHERE mushaf_id = ? AND page_number = ? ORDER BY position_in_page`): plan is a Bitmap Index Scan on index_mushaf_words_on_mushaf_id_and_word_id (all 83,668 rows of the mushaf) then Bitmap Heap Scan filtering page_number (~83,500 rows removed, ~3,900 heap blocks), then a quicksort. V2 (mushaf 1): first touch 11.5 ms (shared hit 4057, read 34), warm 10-12 ms. 9-line IndoPak (mushaf 29, 1890 pages): first touch 23.4 ms (shared read 2264), warm 8-10 ms. MushafLayouts::Page#lines (both DBs, AR objects): first call 63 ms (connection and AR warm-up), warm 11-13 ms. Whole request with dev SSR: 25-28 ms in Rails, ~47 ms round trip. 'Cold' is Postgres-buffer cold only; the OS page cache was not dropped.

AC3 resolver: app/services/fonts/url_resolver.rb (Fonts::UrlResolver, pure Ruby) with standalone test test/services/fonts/url_resolver_test.rb (9 runs, 24 assertions). One-off sweep over every published font resource (all 604 pages for per-page fonts), the per-page fonts of v1, v2 and v4-tajweed for pages 1-604 in every format, every published layout's and script's font, and the decoration fonts: 5,488 unique URLs, 5,484 answered 200. No working URL: font resource 575 'Arabic Sign Language Font' (meta paths arabic-sign/arabic_sign_font.* are 404 in all three formats; the old stylesheet's sign-language/sign-language.* files answer 200), and quran_fonts/v4-tajweed/woff2/p328.woff2 (404; the woff and ttf of p328 answer 200 and are the next @font-face sources). No font at all: layout 569 (SVG mushaf, code svg) and scripts 49 and 50 (image scripts).

AC4 unicode layouts: Mushaf Qatar (layout 570, Madani, qpc-hafs) pages 50 and 603, IndoPak 15 lines (layout 12) pages 2 and 255, and IndoPak 16 lines (layout 11) page 187 (combined surah-name + bismillah line): surah-name, bismillah and centred lines are placed from mushaf_line_alignments, and the DOM comparison with the old preview matched lines, line kinds (surah/bismillah/center/justified) and glyphs on all five pages. Surah-opening screenshots: side-570-p603.png, side-12-p255.png, side-11-p187.png in the builder's scratchpad shots/ folder.

Request spec spec/requests/dev/mushaf_pages_spec.rb (6 examples): V2 page 2 props (surah line with surahNumber 2, bismillah line centred, word count equals the mushaf_words count, font p2.woff2 first), combined surah+bismillah line on layout 11 page 187, clamp 610 → 604 on Mushaf Qatar, V4 layout taken from the `mushaf` meta key with woff2/woff/truetype sources, SVG layout with textFont null and no lines, 404 for a font resource id. SSR test MushafPage.ssr.test.tsx. Final narrow runs: `bundle exec rspec` 22 examples 0 failures, url_resolver_test 9 runs 0 failures, typelizer:check up to date, yarn typecheck, test:frontend 5 passed, lint:frontend and format:frontend clean. bin/gate not run (driver-owned).
decisions: One font URL rule (Fonts::UrlResolver): a font is base paths per format under <CDN_HOST>/qul/fonts/, file = path + '.' + format; a path whose last segment equals its format (quran_fonts/v2/woff2) is a per-page folder → <path>/p<page>.<ext>. Sources in browser order woff2, woff, ttf, otf. This detects page fonts from the path, not from font-face (the V4 Tajweed font resource has no font-face, which is how the old partial built quran_fonts/v4-tajweed/woff2.woff2). from_meta(meta, page:) serves font resources; named(code, page:) serves layout font codes (mushafs.default_font_name), script fonts (for_script: font-face, else the first choice of 'a or b' in the font key) and the decoration fonts surah-name-v4, quran-common and bismillah. The NAMED table copies the paths the old stylesheets load for each code; no field links a layout to its font resource, and some codes have no matching font resource (indopak-nastaleeq loads nastaleeq/indopak-nastaleeq-waqf-lazim, digitalkhatt's resource has font-face 'digitalkhaat'). Recommendation: once 001-07 links layouts and scripts to font resources, resolve through from_meta and shrink NAMED.

The old builders (ResourcePresenter#build_font_assets, shared/_resource_font_face) are protected old code and were not touched; the new pages use the resolver instead. Family names are new ('v2-p300', 'qpc-hafs'), not the old p300-v2 classes.

Page query is `mushaf_id = ? AND page_number = ? ORDER BY position_in_page` with no new index. A faster plan via mushaf_pages first/last verse range (0.5-1 ms, index_on_mushaf_word_position) was rejected: mushaf 20 (Digital Khatt) has 361 words outside its page's verse range.

Words are ordered by position_in_page, then grouped by verse within a line in first-appearance order, exactly as the old preview does. position_in_line is wrong for many lines' first word (1/2/6/7/14/19/20: thousands of lines), and position_in_page puts a verse's waqf mark after the next verse's first word in 2,203 places in mushaf 6 (also 136 in 14, 2 in 7).
Lines with neither words nor an alignment row are dropped; the old view renders them as empty zero-height divs, so nothing visible changes.

Glyph page fonts use font-display: block (private-use glyphs must not show in a fallback font); other fonts use swap. Only the shown page's font is emitted, with no preload. The V4 'light' palette from _page_font.html.erb is applied with @font-palette-values; tajweed colours match the old preview.
CSS is emitted with <style dangerouslySetInnerHTML> because React escapes quotes in <style> text children. Every string in it currently comes from the resolver's NAMED constants.

Lines are white-space: nowrap inside a w-max page, so the browser can never add a line break; justified lines use text-align-last: justify. Header sizes (70px frame, 50px name), 30px text, line-height 1.85 and blue ayah-end marks copy the old computed styles.

config/initializers/typelizer.rb sets types_import_path '@/types/serializers' (the default '@/types' does not resolve); this rewrote the digest line of the existing generated files. Inline Alba association blocks have no typelize, so FontSourceResource is its own serializer.

Screenshots and DOM comparisons were taken with the Playwright-cached headless Chrome driven over CDP from a scratch script (no committed browser harness exists yet; 001-05 adds it). Rails ran in qul-dev, Vite on the host, as in AGENTS.md.
concerns: Font resource 575 'Arabic Sign Language Font' has meta paths (arabic-sign/arabic_sign_font.*) that are 404 in every format; working files are at sign-language/sign-language.*. This is a data fix on the content row (not done: the content DB is not changed by this sprint). quran_fonts/v4-tajweed/woff2/p328.woff2 is 404 on the CDN; browsers fall back to the p328 woff/ttf sources, so page 328 still renders.

Fallbacks for 001-15 (S4 passed for V1, V2, V4): layout 569 (SVG mushaf) has no font and no word rows → explicit 'no preview' state; image layouts (code img, none published) and image scripts 49 and 50 have no font. For a missing page font, use the unicode text of the page with a notice; V4 colour can fall back to the V2 page font (same glyph codes in mushaf_words).

When 001-15 resolves fonts from admin-edited meta (from_meta), family and path strings go into the <style> block unescaped; a quote or </style> in meta would break out. Sanitise families and paths (e.g. allow only [\w/.-]) before rendering them as CSS.
IndoPak waqf marks render with a visible space before them on the new page, attached in the old preview (side-12-p255.png, side-11-p187.png). Same glyphs and lines; spacing to fix in 001-15.
Vertical spacing around surah headers and bismillah lines differs from the old preview (cosmetic). Layout width is the widest line, not a fixed page width.

Typelizer types word text, charTypeName, verseId, fontCode and name as non-null. The published layouts' mushaf_words have no NULLs in those columns (checked), but the columns are nullable. Mushafs with lines_per_page NULL or a layout without a resource content row would error (none exist among published layouts).

'Cold' timings are Postgres-buffer cold only (OS page cache not dropped). Production hardware and concurrency not measured. Warm cost ~10 ms per page query; caching per (mushaf, page) would be cheap if 001-15 needs it.

QUL_INERTIA_SAMPLE_PAGE=true now also exposes /__dev/mushaf_pages/:id (read-only, published layouts only, no auth). docker/README.md still describes the flag as adding only the sample page (docker/ is protected, not edited).

stories.title: Vertical slice: type pages on real data behind the page group setting
stories.description: Build one real page end to end so every layer and its conventions exist before breadth: `/resources/{type}` for all 14 types, in a first form (type description and a card per published resource, from fields that exist on main). The slice establishes and documents by example: the page group setting and how a group takes over an existing URL and falls back to the old view; the Inertia base controller (layout, shared props, error rendering); a catalog query object and Alba serializers with no dependency on controllers or the session; generated types used by the page; server-managed title, description, Open Graph, Twitter, canonical and JSON-LD; GA4 page views on first load and on every Inertia visit; browser error reporting; a 404 Inertia page with the right status; the catalog taxonomy (type labels, descriptions, categories) kept in one server-side file and sent as props; and the Playwright harness running against real Rails on a clone. Only the components this page needs are ported from the prototype; 001-11 ports the rest. Out of scope: status, which-to-pick and comparison tables (001-13), the shell beyond a minimal frame (001-11).
acceptanceCriteria: With `catalog` in the page group setting, GET `/resources/{type}` renders the Inertia component for each of the 14 types with one card per published resource of that type. Evidence: a request spec that compares card counts to a direct count per type.
With `catalog` not in the setting, the same URLs render the old ERB view. Evidence: a request spec for both states.
An unknown type returns status 404 with the Inertia error page in the new layout. Evidence: a request spec and a Playwright check.

The first response's HTML contains the type name and at least one resource name (SSR), plus title, meta description, canonical link on the production host, Open Graph and Twitter tags and a JSON-LD script that parses. Evidence: a request spec on the raw HTML.

stories.description: Give the integration branch its own CI, so every push and pull request to `qul-next` and to sprint branches is checked without the snapshot. acceptanceCriteria: A new workflow file under `.github/workflows/` triggers on push and pull request for `qul-next` and `sprint/**` only, never for `main`. Evidence: the trigger block quoted in the handoff, and `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) -- .github/workflows/tests.yml .github/workflows/deploy.yml .github/workflows/codeql.yml .github/workflows/issue-triage.yml` is empty.

stories.notes: Prescriptive: (1) One new file, for example `.github/workflows/qul-next.yml`; do not edit the four existing workflows (`tests.yml`, `deploy.yml`, `codeql.yml`, `issue-triage.yml`). `tests.yml` already runs on every pull request, so PRs to `qul-next` get the standalone tests from it; do not repeat them here. `deploy.yml` deploys on every push to `main`, which is why the new workflow must never target `main`. (4) Use `.node-version` for Node and yarn classic with `--frozen-lockfile`; install devDependencies (do not set `NODE_ENV=production` for the install step). stories.title: Catalog schema and mechanical backfills
stories.description: Add the catalog fields and clean the link data, each as a CMS-database migration plus an idempotent backfill that replays on a newer copy of the data. Fields: lifecycle status (stable, beta, legacy, superseded; default stable) with a superseded-by pointer; a separate `recommended` flag (false by default), because endorsement is not a lifecycle stage: a recommended resource is still stable and must match a status filter of stable; `script_family` (madani, indopak, other) and rendering method (unicode text plus font, glyph per page, image, svg), both empty by default; a relation type on related-resource links (requires, pairs with, alternative, supersedes) with every existing link set to pairs with; a display name; the review column (empty). Backfills in this story are the deterministic ones: a unique slug for every resource, display names for names that repeat inside a type, removal of the duplicate link, the orphaned link and the orphaned taggings. New resources get a slug when they are created. One task runs every backfill in order. Out of scope: inferred values (001-08), download counters (001-10).
acceptanceCriteria: After migrate plus backfill on a clone, every resource has a non-empty slug, slugs are unique, none is all digits, and the slugs that existed before are unchanged. Evidence: a named spec with the four aggregate queries.

Inside each type, no two published resources share a display name, and `name` is unchanged on every row. Evidence: a spec that groups by type and display name, and a checksum of `name` before and after.

Related links: no duplicate pair and no link with a missing end remain; every remaining link has relation type pairs with. Taggings: none points at a missing resource. Evidence: aggregate queries in a spec.
Running the backfill task a second time changes 0 rows. Evidence: the task's own changed-row report for both runs.
A resource created through the model without a slug gets one; a resource whose name would give an all-digit or taken slug gets a distinct valid one. Evidence: named model specs.
`find_by_slug_or_id!` still resolves an old numeric id. Evidence: a request spec on an old id URL.
No migration adds a constraint that a current production row could violate before the backfill has run. Evidence: migrate succeeds on a fresh clone before any backfill, shown in the handoff.
`git diff db/schema.rb` contains only this story's tables and columns. Evidence: the diff stat.
stories.notes: Read `../qul-data/audit-2026-11-02.md` sections 1, 2, 5 and 8 first. Key the backfills on stable fields (existing slug, resource content id), never on row position, and never write a field a person has set. One slug is an empty string: normalize it to NULL first. Display-name sources: recitations take the style and the surah/ayah kind from the content database (two recitation rows there carry the proper name when the content row's name is blank); scripts take the granularity; translations and tafsirs take the language. Two resources share one content row. Migrations use the CMS connection only. Keep the edit to `app/models/downloadable_resource.rb` to a single `include` line and put the behaviour in a concern: qiraat changes that model. After `db:migrate`, commit only your own `db/schema.rb` lines. Remake the test clones after migrating. Slugs become public URLs and next sprint's API ids: prefer readable, stable forms.

Both reversible `change` migrations, CMS connection only.

Every new column is nullable or has a default, the slug unique index already existed, and no unique index on link pairs was added.

`bin/rails catalog:backfill` (lib/tasks/catalog.rake → Catalog::Backfill.run, one transaction, steps in order blank_slugs, display_names, slugs, related_links, taggings). Dev clone run 1: blank_slugs 1, display_names 54, slugs 538, related_links 2, taggings 21, total 616. Runs 2 and 3: every step 0, total 0.

Display names (app/services/catalog/backfill/display_names.rb): resources whose effective name repeats inside a type get `name (qualifiers)` with only the qualifiers that differ inside the group: recitation style (content DB recitations/audio_recitations → recitation_styles) and granularity; language (CMS language_id, else the content row's) and granularity for translation/tafsir/transliteration/surah-info; granularity otherwise. Members the data cannot tell apart get a counter in id order (`Adel Kalbani (2)`); the first keeps display_name NULL. Never overwrites a set display_name.
`DownloadableResource#display_name` (CatalogFields concern) returns the column or falls back to `name`, so serializers read one method; `name` is never written.

Slugs (Catalog::Slugs.generate): display name parameterized; if taken or all digits, `<base>-<resource_type>`; then `<base>-<type>-N`. Backfill keeps all 26 existing non-blank slugs, normalizes the one '' to NULL first, and fills the other 538 in id order. Model: `normalizes :slug` (blank → nil), `before_validation :assign_slug` when slug is nil, format validation refuses all-digit slugs.

Related links: orphaned rows (either end NULL or missing) deleted, then repeated pairs deleted keeping MIN(id). DownloadableRelatedResource gains `enum :relation_type` (validate: true) and a pair uniqueness validation. Taggings whose resource or tag no longer exists deleted.

CatalogFields concern also: enums status (validate), script_family and rendering (prefix: true, allow nil), belongs_to :superseded_by, and before_destroy deleting the resource's taggings and links in both directions so new orphans are not created. downloadable_resource.rb gains only `include CatalogFields`.

The review column is named `review` (jsonb, default {}), per the PRD's term 'review column'. 001-08 fills it.

assign_slug runs on any save with a blank slug (not only create), so clearing the slug in the CMS form gives a fresh one instead of leaving the resource slugless.
No unique index on (downloadable_resource_id, related_resource_id): it would fail on production before the backfill; a model validation guards new rows instead.

stories.title: Drafted values, review column and review report
stories.description: Infer the values that no field holds today and record them as drafted values. Backfills infer: status (including superseded and its pointer where the data shows a newer version), the `recommended` flag, script family and rendering for script, font and layout resources, requires-links from a layout to its font and from a glyph script to its font, and a one-line summary where none exists. Every inferred field and link is recorded in the review column on the source resource with the backfill name and time. Changing a drafted field outside a backfill clears its entry (a model rule, so it holds for any later editing screen), and a task marks a resource's drafted values, or one field, as reviewed. CMS form changes are deferred by user decision: this sprint the data team works from the review report and a developer applies corrections with the task. A backfill never overwrites a value that is not currently drafted by itself. A task generates the review report: every drafted value, plus the known data errors from the audit that visitors could see. Serializers expose, per field, whether the value is reviewed. Out of scope: how pages show it (001-13, 001-14).
acceptanceCriteria: Each inference rule has table-driven specs written first: given the fields of a resource, it returns the value or no value. Evidence: the named spec file and its example count.

No resource has the `recommended` flag drafted unless the rule's stated evidence holds for it, at most one layout and one font per script family is drafted as recommended, and no legacy or superseded resource is recommended. Evidence: a spec over the clone and the rule text in the handoff.
After the backfill, every value it wrote has an entry in the review column, and every entry in the review column matches a value it wrote. Evidence: a consistency spec over the clone.

Changing a drafted field through the model outside a backfill clears that field's entry, the mark-reviewed task clears entries without changing values, and the next backfill run leaves both in place. Evidence: model and task specs for the three steps.
A second backfill run changes 0 rows. Evidence: the changed-row report.

The review report task writes a file under `tmp/` whose drafted-value row count equals the number of review-column entries, and which has a section for each known data error class. Evidence: the two counts in the handoff. The file itself is not committed and not pasted.

The resource serializer carries the status, the `recommended` flag, script family, rendering, summary and typed relations with a reviewed flag for each drafted field, and the generated TypeScript types include them. Evidence: a serializer spec and the drift check.
stories.notes: Read the audit sections 4, 5, 7 and 12 and the gap table in `../qul-redesign/research/data-requirements.html`. Draft conservatively: which layout or font is the default per script family is a scholarly and product call the data cannot answer, and popularity is not authority. Sources: layout facts and font names come from the content database (`mushafs`, resource-content meta keys such as `text-type`, `font`, `mushaf`); no field links a layout to its font, the link is implied by font names. The glyph layouts use per-page font sets. Summaries are templated from type, language, granularity and format facts; never claim anything the fields do not show, and say nothing about recitation style or qira'at that the content rows do not state. The report must not include data source names or any user-related field (see the private sprint notes). The data-model change is recorded in the decision log by 001-19; flag here anything the maintainers must agree to. Do not change the ActiveAdmin forms in this sprint (user decision); the existing CMS form must keep saving a resource without touching the new fields. The correction path is the mark-reviewed task and model writes; document both in the review report's header.

done: Inference rules (app/services/catalog/inference.rb, pure Ruby): script_family, rendering, status, recommended, required_font, summary over Catalog::Inference::Facts. Table-driven standalone test test/services/catalog/inference_test.rb written first and watched red (8 failures on a stub), then green: 8 runs, 97 assertions (20 script-family rows, 16 rendering rows, 10 status rows, 17 recommended rows, 15 required-font rows, 18 summary rows plus a length test).

Six drafting steps appended to Catalog::Backfill::STEPS in this order: script_families, renderings, statuses, requires_links, recommended, summaries. Facts are loaded per step by Backfill::Facts (CMS rows with tags, files and links; content rows, languages and mushafs in separate queries; mushaf via MushafLayouts::Page.mushaf_for). stories.title: Catalog search query, facets and spotlight endpoint
stories.description: Build the query object behind `/resources` and the spotlight, and the `/resources` controller action that serves it as Inertia props. One input shape (text, type, language, several script families, format, granularity, status, sort, page) gives results, a total and facet counts. Text search is Unicode-aware and matches Arabic. The query object loads the published catalog once (a few hundred rows with their tags, plus language names resolved from the content database in a second step), then normalizes, filters, counts facets, sorts and pages in Ruby: no Postgres extension and no SQL per facet. Sort is popular (signed-in plus anonymous downloads), name or updated. Each facet's counts reflect the other active filters. File type strings map to a small format vocabulary in the server-side taxonomy. The spotlight gets a small same-origin JSON endpoint that uses the same query object and a slim serializer; it is internal, unversioned and not a public API. Vocabularies that do not change per request are sent so the client fetches them once. Out of scope: the React page (001-12).
acceptanceCriteria: Specs written first cover: an Arabic query matches a resource through its name, its tags or its language's native name, with and without diacritics (where the clone has no such row, the spec creates one inside its transaction); a Latin query is case- and accent-insensitive; a language name finds its translations; an empty query returns everything published.

Each filter alone and two script families together return exactly the rows a direct query returns on the clone; a status filter of stable includes the resources flagged `recommended`. Evidence: named specs per filter.

The text normalizer has table-driven specs: Latin accents, case, Arabic harakat, tatweel and the alef, ya and ta marbuta variants all fold to the same key on both the query and the indexed text. Evidence: the named spec file and its example count.
For each facet, the count shown for a value equals the result total after selecting that value. Evidence: a property-style spec that samples values on the clone.
Popular order equals the order of the combined download totals from a direct aggregate query; unpublished resources and files never appear or count. Evidence: named specs.

GET `/resources?…` with the `catalog` group on returns the Inertia component with results, facets and the echoed filters; an invalid filter value is ignored, not a 500. Evidence: request specs with `have_props`.
The spotlight endpoint returns at most a fixed small number of results as JSON for a query and sets `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. Evidence: a request spec.
The whole catalog request runs the same fixed number of queries whatever the filters, facets and result count. Evidence: a query-count assertion in a spec, run with no filter and with several.
stories.notes: Do not reuse or extend `Resources::SearchQuery`: it strips non-Latin characters and is tied to the old views. Filter in Ruby, not SQL (user decision at plan review): the CMS schema enables no extension (`unaccent` and `pg_trgm` are absent), the text to match lives in two databases, and every facet needs counts under the other active filters. Over a few hundred rows that is one load plus plain Ruby, and facet counts are tallies. All filter fields are on CMS rows; language and reciter names live in the content database, so load them in a second step keyed by id instead of joining. Normalize the query and the indexed text with one small module: Unicode decomposition, strip combining marks (this covers Latin accents and Arabic harakat), drop tatweel, fold alef, ya and ta marbuta variants, downcase. Do not keep the loaded catalog between requests (the development and test cache stores keep nothing). If the catalog grows into the thousands, filtering moves into SQL behind the same interface. The anonymous counter arrives in 001-10: read the combined total through one method that 001-10 completes. Some translations have no language on the CMS row but have one on the content row. Granularity is `cardinality_type`, set on every row. `/search` already exists and is Quran text search: do not take that path. Keep the endpoint out of `/api`. This query object is what the public API will call next sprint: no `params`, no `current_user`, no Inertia types inside it.

It loads published resources + tags, published files (CMS) and content-row language ids + languages (content DB, keyed by id), then searches, filters, tallies facets, sorts and pages in Ruby. Nothing cached. FACETS = type language script format granularity status; facets[f] is {value => count} under the other filters (selected values kept with 0), most results first.

Search text per row: display name, name, type label and title, language name and native name, tag names; every query word must be a substring.

Spotlight path is /spotlight, not /resources/spotlight: under /resources it would collide with /resources/:type (and with the old /resources/:id when the group is off). It is outside the page-group constraints because every new page carries the spotlight whatever groups are on. Not under /api.

Facet counts are 'results if you select this value instead' (each facet ignores its own selection). For the multi-select script family that is the count of that family alone, which is what the property spec checks.

Result cards use a new SearchResultResource over the query rows rather than ResourceCardResource (which reads associations the query does not preload); name is display_name so duplicate names inside a type are told apart.
The test clone has no script families (backfills are not replayed there), so the script-family filter and facet specs set a few rows inside the transaction.

stories.title: Downloads: one route, two modes, counted
stories.description: Give file downloads one route with server-side rules, a download mode setting, and counting that covers every download. Rules in both modes: 404 for an unpublished file or a file of an unpublished resource; a restricted resource is blocked for everyone except admins. Sign-in mode: an anonymous request is sent to sign-in and returns to the resource page, where the download starts. Public mode: the file is sent without an account. The new URL is built from the resource slug and the file, with no file token; the existing token URL keeps working and follows the same rules. Counting: a signed-in download writes the per-user row as today; an anonymous download adds 1 to an anonymous counter column on the file with one atomic update. There is no visitor cookie, no deduplication and no per-visitor row: nothing about the visitor is read or stored. Existing totals are kept; one method returns the combined total that popular sorting reads. Download paths are disallowed in `robots.txt` and their responses are marked noindex, so well-behaved crawlers do not add to the counts. Out of scope: the files panel UI (001-14), storage changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Request specs written first, for both routes and both modes: unpublished file gives 404; file of an unpublished resource gives 404; restricted resource gives a blocked response for an anonymous user and a normal user, and a redirect to the file for an admin; unknown file gives 404.

Sign-in mode: an anonymous request redirects to sign-in, and after sign-in the user lands on the resource page with the download started. Evidence: a request spec for the redirect chain and a Playwright test added once 001-14 exists (note it in the handoff if deferred).
Public mode: an anonymous GET redirects to the file and adds exactly 1 to the file's anonymous count every time; a HEAD request adds 0. Evidence: named specs.

An anonymous download sets no cookie of its own, and its only database write is the counter increment: no row is added to any table. Evidence: a spec on the Set-Cookie header and on the row counts of `user_downloads` and any table this story adds.

A signed-in download creates or increments the per-user row and does not reduce or reset the anonymous count; two concurrent signed-in downloads both count, and two concurrent anonymous downloads both count. Evidence: named specs, with threads.

`robots.txt` disallows both download path patterns for every user agent, and both download responses carry `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. Evidence: a request spec for the header and the file's lines quoted.
The combined total for every file after the migration equals the total before it. Evidence: aggregate comparison on a clone, as a single equality in the handoff.
The setting defaults to `sign_in` and an unknown value fails at boot. Evidence: a spec.
stories.notes: Read the private sprint notes (team drop) before starting: they describe today's behaviour and what must change. The redirect target is the file's storage URL; without the storage variables the URL host is wrong locally, so specs assert the redirect, not the fetch. Update emails and the profile download list read the per-user rows: keep writing them. Anonymous counting is a plain counter (user decision at plan review; it replaces the earlier cookie-per-day deduplication): one atomic `UPDATE … SET column = column + 1` (`update_counters`), never read-modify-write and never the cache. No cookie, no visitor id, no address, no user agent. Signed-in downloads are not deduplicated today either (each one increments the per-user row), so both totals mean download requests. `DownloadableFile#track_download` recomputes `download_count` from the per-user rows, so the anonymous number lives in its own column where that recount cannot erase it. Known cost, accepted: repeated requests and scripts count every time; say so where the totals are documented. `public/robots.txt` today has a `Disallow` line with no `User-agent` line above it, so it has no effect: add the `User-agent: *` line when adding the download rules. The old token route is `ResourcesController#download` behind `authenticate_user!`. Do not edit that controller: declare the same path in the sprint's routes block above the old `resources :resources` block so it reaches the new download controller first, and both URLs share one code path. This is the one change to an old route this sprint makes. Why no token in the new URL: access is decided by the server rules and not by the URL, the public API will hand out these links next sprint, and a slug-plus-file URL is readable and stable; check how exports replace file rows before choosing what identifies a file in the URL. Admin means the existing role check; do not add a new permission model. The download link is a plain link, not an Inertia visit, because it ends in a redirect to another host.

stories.title: Catalog page and spotlight
stories.description: Build `/resources` from v7 on the props from 001-09, and the ⌘K spotlight. Filter changes are Inertia visits that keep scroll and local state and reload only what changed. On phones the filters open in a bottom drawer. Spotlight: opens from the header icon and from ⌘K or Ctrl K on any new page, searches resources through the JSON endpoint as the user types, is keyboard-navigable, and goes to the chosen resource or to the full catalog results.
acceptanceCriteria: Loading a URL with a query, two script families, a format and a sort renders exactly that view on the server, with the controls showing those values. Evidence: a request spec on the SSR HTML and a Playwright test.

Changing a filter updates the URL and the results without a full page load, and the request asks only for the props that change. Evidence: a Playwright test that inspects the Inertia partial-reload headers.
Back and Forward restore the earlier filter state. Evidence: a Playwright test.
Typing a language's native name in Arabic script returns that language's resources in the page. Evidence: a Playwright test on the clone.
At 390 px the filters are in a bottom drawer that opens, applies and closes; the page has no horizontal scroll. Evidence: a Playwright test.
A filter combination with no results shows the empty state and the request card, whose link opens the issue form URL. Evidence: a Playwright test.

The spotlight opens with the keyboard shortcut and the icon on a type page and on the catalog, shows results for a typed query, moves with arrow keys, opens a result with Enter and closes with Escape, restoring focus. Typing fast sends no more than one request per pause and never shows results for an older query. Evidence: Playwright tests, one with request counting.
The catalog page has title, description and canonical tags; filtered views have a canonical that points to the unfiltered page or are marked noindex. Evidence: a request spec.
stories.notes: The prototype catalog (`ds/src/app/pages/catalog.tsx`) filters mock data in the browser and parses the hash; keep its layout, replace its data flow. The docs do not spell out the search recipe: same-URL visits replace history by default, so decide deliberately which changes push a history entry (filter toggles) and which replace (typing). The key hint shows ⌘K or Ctrl K by platform; render a neutral label on the server and set it after mount to avoid a hydration mismatch. acceptanceCriteria: A sweep spec requests the detail page of every published resource on the clone with SSR errors raised: all return 200, including the resources with no files, on unapproved content rows, with no word rows and with blank content names. Evidence: the spec output with the count.
An id URL and a URL with the wrong type return 301 to the slug URL; an unknown slug and an unpublished resource return 404 with the error page. Evidence: request specs.

The files panel shows, per file, a format label, a human-readable download size and the checksum; sizes equal the stored byte sizes. Evidence: a request spec on props and a Vitest test of the formatting.

Sign-in mode: an anonymous visitor who clicks Download signs in as the fake user and ends on the same resource page with the download started and one per-user row written. Public mode: the click downloads without sign-in and the sign-in offer is visible. Evidence: Playwright tests for both modes.

stories.notes: File facts come from ActiveStorage blobs: every file is an archive, so the size is the download size; the checksum is base64 MD5, show it labelled as MD5 (hex) and do not call it SHA; `content_type` is unreliable, use the file type string mapped by the taxonomy. stories.title: Mushaf page, font and script previews
stories.description: Fill the Preview tab for layouts, fonts and scripts, using what 001-04 proved. Layouts: one rendered mushaf page with page navigation (previous, next, jump to page, jump to surah), for unicode layouts and for the glyph-per-page layouts, with lines placed as in the print. Fonts: a sample in the font itself, plus the glyph and ligature views the old font page offers in its Ligatures and Glyphs tabs, for the fonts that have them. Scripts: a sample of a chosen ayah range in the script's own font. Data arrives as a deferred prop keyed by the page or surah in the query string, and navigation reloads only that prop, so a page view is shareable and nothing loads the whole resource. One preview interface on the server, with one provider per kind, that the public API can reuse. Layouts or fonts that cannot be rendered show an explicit state, never an error.
acceptanceCriteria: For every published layout, page 1, a middle page and the last page render, or the layout shows the explicit "no preview" state. Evidence: a Playwright sweep with the per-layout result table in the handoff.
Page navigation changes the query string, requests only the preview prop, and loads only the fonts of the page shown. Evidence: a Playwright test that inspects request headers and font requests.
A direct load of a URL with a page number renders that page; a page number beyond the page count is clamped or gives the page's own not-found state, not a 500. Evidence: request specs.
The glyph-per-page layouts match the old preview on the four pages from 001-04. Evidence: screenshots compared in the handoff.
Every published font shows a sample rendered in that font once the font has loaded, or the explicit state with the reason. Evidence: a Playwright sweep using `document.fonts.check`.
Every published script shows its sample for a chosen surah in the right font, for both word-level and ayah-level scripts. Evidence: a Playwright sweep and request specs on the props.

Each font whose old page has a Ligatures or Glyphs tab shows the same glyph and ligature sets in the new preview, and the old tab URLs redirect to that view. Evidence: a request spec on the props compared with what the old tab renders for one font of each kind, and a Playwright check.
The preview provider for layouts loads in a plain Ruby spec without a controller, and the page query count is bounded. Evidence: named specs.
stories.notes: Use the font URL resolver from 001-04; do not call `ResourcePresenter#build_font_assets` or `shared/_resource_font_face`. The old previews (`app/views/resources/previews/`) query inside ERB and several show global data instead of the resource's own: use them as a behaviour reference only, and do not edit them (qiraat changes two of them). Font and script resources have no per-resource sample rows; samples are Quran text in the right encoding from the content database. Inject per-page `@font-face` rules in a way that works under SSR and does not accumulate rules as the user pages. Respect the fallbacks the spike recorded.
