decisions: One interface for every kind: Previews.for returns a Data value that names its own serializer; the deferred prop is Previews.as_json(Previews.for(page.resource, preview_query)). Nil means the type has no provider yet (the frontend shows the general 'No preview for this resource yet'). Unavailable carries the reason (SVG layout, unknown script text type, font without files).

Navigation is router.get with only: ['preview'] to the slug URL with the preview keys, so the URL is shareable and Back works. Font views (sample/ligatures/glyphs) switch on the client, like the page tabs: the ligatures and the font files are already in the prop.

Per-page @font-face rules live in a <style> inside the preview component, re-rendered per page, so old rules disappear and only the shown page's files load. The decoration fonts are emitted only when the page has surah-name or bismillah lines. The V4 palette is one @font-palette-values rule listing every V4 family, because a later rule with the same name replaces an earlier one (several V4 page fonts can be on screen in a script range).

Script font: the published font resource whose `script` meta names the script's text type (gives DK V2 for text_digital_khatt and DK IndoPak for text_digital_khatt_indopak, matching the old helper), else the resolver's for_script(meta). Imlaei scripts therefore use me_quran (first choice in their meta), not qpc-hafs as the old helper did.

Glyph scripts (code_v1/v2/v4) are drawn word by word even at ayah level: an ayah can cross pages and each page's glyphs exist only in that page's font. code_v4 has no column; it uses the code_v2 glyph codes with the V4 page font at v2_page (the codes match mushaf 19's words). The old preview read a nonexistent code_v4 column and showed nothing.

Image scripts (49, 50) show each word's image from Word#<text-type> instead of 'no preview'. The tajweed text is sanitized to <rule class> tags on the server and coloured with the old tajweed-new colours.

Font sample text: the Verse column the font's `script` meta names (Al-Fatihah), else the editor's `text` meta, else the column of a Quran script linked to the font in either direction, else text_uthmani. The page fonts (V1/V2/V4) show their mushaf page (the enabled mushaf whose default_font_name matches the font's page folder). This avoids the requires links, which the test clone may lack. A tajweed column is never used for a sample.
The 001-04 spike page was deleted instead of kept beside the real preview, so mushaf rendering has one implementation.
Preview components live in components/previews (not the ui/qul kit), so they need no kit.tsx fixtures. They have their own Vitest and SSR tests.
The client does not clamp jump-to-page: the number input's min/max stops the form, and the server clamps anyway.
concerns: The URL can disagree with what the server shows after it falls back: ?page=99999 shows page 604 and ?view=ligatures on a font without ligatures shows the sample, but the URL keeps the value. Cosmetic, and a reload corrects it.

Qira'at scripts (581/582) use the Hafs Verse table for surah lengths and keys. Warsh numbering differs, so some ranges can show ayahs whose rows are missing or keyed differently. On the clone, Al-Fatihah and Al-Ikhlas render.
The family name of font 242 is 'font' (the resolver takes the basename of nastaleeq/Hanafi/…/font). It works, but a later sanitised font-face would read better.
The new mushaf page is as wide as its widest line, while the old page was a wider fixed width with justified lines. The IndoPak waqf-mark spacing from the 001-04 concern was not changed or rechecked.

Phone width: the surah header frame on glyph pages can be wider than the text block, and the page card scrolls horizontally when it is (overflow-x-auto). The sweeps ran on desktop only; the navigation, ligature and glyph tests also ran on phone.
The glyph grid fetches the TTF from static-cdn.tarteel.ai with fetch(). It worked from localhost (the CDN allows CORS), but this was not checked from the production origin.
The review fixes (string-only query values, no tajweed font sample) were verified by request specs, not by a browser rerun.
RuboCop cannot run here. Ruby lines are kept under 120 characters by hand.

stories.title: Audio, text and record-sample previews
stories.description: Fill the Preview tab for the remaining types through the same preview interface as 001-15. Recitations: an audio player for a chosen surah (or ayah, for ayah-by-ayah recitations) that highlights the ayah being recited from segment data where the recitation has segments, and plays without highlighting where it has none. Translations, tafsirs and transliterations: the text of a chosen surah, with footnotes where present and correct direction and language attributes. Every other type (surah info, ayah themes, ayah topics, similar ayahs, mutashabihat, morphology, Quran metadata): a small, bounded sample of the resource's own records, or the explicit "no preview" state where the resource has no per-resource sample data. The chosen surah is in the query string and only the preview prop reloads.
acceptanceCriteria: For a recitation with segments, during playback the highlighted ayah changes at the segment boundary times. Evidence: a Vitest test of the highlight logic against recorded segment data with a fake clock, and a Playwright test that seeks and checks the highlight.
A recitation without segments plays and shows no highlight and no error. Evidence: a Playwright test.
A sweep over every published recitation, translation, tafsir and transliteration returns preview props for surah 1 and surah 114 without error. Evidence: a spec with counts.
A right-to-left translation renders with `dir="rtl"` and its language code; a left-to-right one with `ltr`. Evidence: a request spec on SSR HTML for one of each.

For each of the remaining types, the preview shows at most a fixed number of records taken from that resource, or the "no preview" state. Evidence: request specs per type on the props, with the bound asserted.
Changing the surah updates the query string and requests only the preview prop. Evidence: a Playwright test.
Tafsir and translation text that contains markup is sanitized on the server. Evidence: a spec with a script tag in the input.
stories.notes: Reuse the finders behind `/api/v1` (`app/finders/v1`) where they fit, called in process, not over HTTP. The v1 segment endpoints are keyed by recitation id, not resource content id; surah recitations and ayah recitations are different tables. `per_page` in v1 is unreliable for small sizes. Several types have no per-resource sample data and their old previews show global data or fail on nil: that is the case for the explicit state. Audio files are on the CDN; the player must not start loading audio until the user asks. Tafsirs can be very long: bound the text per request (a surah may need paging by ayah range). Some languages have no native name or direction; default sensibly.

done: Server: three new providers behind Previews.for, each one `when` in Previews.provider. Every one of the 14 catalog types now has a provider (previews_spec asserts that against Catalog::Taxonomy::TYPES). Previews::Recitation (kind 'recitation'): one surah (?surah=). A surah-by-surah recitation has one track (Audio::ChapterAudioFile.audio_url) and ayah times from Audio::Segment timestamp_from/to, keyed by audio_recitation_id + chapter like V1::SegmentFinder. An ayah-by-ayah recitation has one track per ayah (AudioFile#audio_url, ::Recitation by resource_content_id). Each ayah carries track/from/to. `highlights` is false for a surah recitation with no segments. A recitation with no audio for the surah is Unavailable. Previews::Text (kind 'text') covers translation, tafsir and transliteration. It uses ?surah/from/to with ranges of 10 (max 20), or 3 (max 5) for tafsirs. Ayah rows come with FootNotes; word-by-word resources use WordTranslation/WordTransliteration (plain text); tafsir entries are the rows overlapping the range, each with its group's ayahs, and `to` extends to the last group's end. Every entry has the ayah Arabic (text_uthmani) and a `locale` {code, direction}. Previews::Records (kind 'records') covers surah-info, ayah-theme, ayah-topics, similar-ayah, mutashabihat, morphology and quran-metadata. It returns at most LIMIT = 10 records, read the way lib/exporter reads them, from the chosen surah for the surah-scoped types.

Shared helpers in app/services/previews.rb: Previews.surahs/surah/range (moved out of Script, which now uses them), Previews::Locale + Previews.locale(content, fallback), Previews.sanitize (SafeListSanitizer, tags p br b strong i em u sup sub span div h1-h6 ul ol li blockquote, attributes lang dir only), Previews.plain, and Previews.excerpt (TEXT_LIMIT 20_000 characters: keeps whole top-level elements and sets `truncated`).

Serializers in app/serializers/previews: RecitationResource, RecitationAyahResource, TextResource, TextEntryResource, TextAyahResource, TextFootnoteResource, TextWordResource, RecordsResource, RecordResource and LocaleResource. The deferred prop's union type now includes them; the types were regenerated and `bin/rails typelizer:check` is up to date.

Frontend app/frontend/components/previews: recitation-player.tsx (exports activeAyah; usePlayer gives <audio preload=none> its src only on Play, reads currentTime every animation frame while playing, plays the tracks in order on `ended`, has per-ayah 'Play from ayah' buttons when times exist, scrolls the active ayah into view, and shows a no-segments note), text-preview.tsx (the lang/dir on each text and footnote, a word grid, a truncated note, 'No text for this ayah'), and records-preview.tsx (an optional surah picker with previous/next surah, the sample size, tags, and an empty state). navigation.tsx gained SurahSelect and AyahRangeToolbar, which ScriptPreview now uses too: surah values are numbers now. preview.tsx dispatches the three kinds, and the player is keyed by its first track so it remounts per surah. A .preview-html block in styles/inertia.css styles the sanitized HTML.

AC1 (highlight at segment boundaries): Vitest recitation-player.test.tsx. activeAyah is checked against recorded Husary Mujawwad Al-Fatihah times (4469→1:1, 4470→none, 4670→1:2, 75389→none). Component tests use fake requestAnimationFrame and a media clock the test sets: the highlight is 1:1 at 4469, none at 4470, 1:2 at 4670, none at 15669 and 1:3 at 15670, and 'Play from ayah 1:5' seeks to 33.045. Playwright previews.spec.ts 'a recitation with segments…' plays the real CDN audio on desktop and phone: no audio request before Play; a seek into ayah 3 highlights 1:3 (aria-current); a seek to 1 s before the end of 1:1 shows 1:1 and then 1:2 once playback crosses the boundary.

AC2: Playwright 'a recitation without segments plays with no highlight and no error' (desktop and phone): data-highlights false and the note shown; it plays past 10 s with no active ayah, no aria-current and no pageerror or console error. Vitest covers the same.

AC3: spec/services/previews/sweep_spec.rb on the test clone: 'Swept 455 resources × 2 surahs: recitation ayah 36, recitation surah 230, tafsir ayah 216, translation ayah 382, translation word 26, transliteration ayah 18, transliteration word 2' (0 unavailable, 0 errors).

AC4: spec/requests/catalog/media_previews_spec.rb renders the real page plus its deferred preview through the SSR bundle (it POSTs the merged page to the SsrServer /render endpoint inside SsrServer.with_ssr, because a deferred prop is never in the first response's SSR HTML). The text divs of an RTL translation carry lang=<iso_code> dir=rtl, and an LTR one carries dir=ltr.

AC5: request specs per type with the bound asserted (records ≤ 10 and limit == 10). Surah info: keys equal that resource's ChapterInfo ids for the surah. Ayah themes: surah 2 has more than 10 themes and returns exactly 10. Ayah topics: 10, the first is Topic.order(:id).first, no surah. Similar ayahs and mutashabihat: 10 for surah 2, labels 2:n. Morphology: word labels 112:n:m and ayah labels 112:n. Quran metadata: first labels Juz 1 / Hizb 1 / 1. Al-Fatihah / 1:1 / Sajdah 1. An unknown morphology kind gives the explicit Unavailable reason.

AC6: Playwright 'changing the surah updates the query string and requests only the preview prop' (desktop and phone). On a translation, the select goes to ?surah=114 with exactly 1 Inertia request (X-Inertia-Partial-Data 'preview') and 114:1 shown. On the segmented recitation, the URL becomes ?surah=114 and the only partial data requested is ['preview'].

AC7: request specs put 'keptlink' into a translation row, a new footnote and a tafsir row. The props hold 'alert(1)keptlink' (the script element, handlers and links are gone; the text is shown escaped). A 400-paragraph tafsir entry is cut to ≤ 20,000 characters at an element boundary, with truncated true.

Baseline before any change (yarn test:browser previews.spec.ts on 001-15's head): 10 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed. The failure was the font sweep on 'QPC V4 Tajweed Font', where document.fonts.check failed for quran-common and surah-name-v4 on its mushaf page. After this story the full previews.spec.ts gave 17 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed, including that font sweep, so the failure looks like font-loading timing, not a regression.

Gates: full RSpec in qul-dev 250 examples, 0 failures after one spec update (the old 'no preview for a type without one yet' example now asserts that every catalog type has a provider), with the test and SSR bundles rebuilt on the host. Vitest: 17 files, 224 tests. typecheck, lint:frontend, format:frontend and eslint/prettier on spec/browser are clean. typelizer:check is up to date. Playwright: previews.spec.ts 17 passed / 3 skipped; resource-page.spec.ts 9 passed / 3 skipped after its tab test was changed to expect the text preview instead of 'No preview for this resource yet'. Look screenshots (recitation, Pashto RTL translation on phone, ayah theme) looked right.
decisions: Records types read what the resource's download holds, mirroring lib/exporter. Most of these exporters (ayah themes, topics, matching ayahs, mutashabihat, morphology, quran metadata) export a whole global table and take the resource content only for the file name. So the sample is the start of that table, or of the chosen surah. The explicit no-preview state is kept for a resource whose records cannot be identified (unknown morphology-resource-type or metadata cardinality). Topics are all Topic rows by id, as the exporter does; the published Topics resource (rc 827) owns no Topic rows itself. Surah info is the only one keyed by resource_content_id.

The same thresholds as the exporters: matching ayahs approved with score ≥ 50; phrases approved with words_count ≥ 3, occurrence > 1, verses_count > 1 and review_status 'new' (the exporter's TODO filter).
Quran metadata is chosen by cardinality_type (1_juz/1_hizb/1_rub/1_manzil/1_ruku/1_chapter/1_ayah/1_sajda), not by the content name the old partials used.

Ayah-by-ayah recitations always highlight: each file is one ayah, so the playing file names the ayah (highlights true, from 0, to null). The 'without segments' case in the criteria is a surah recitation with no Audio::Segment rows; on the clone that applies to 68 of the 115 surah recitations for Al-Fatihah.

The highlight is per ayah, not per word. The old player's word highlight and range repeat were left out as out of scope. Surah segment times come from Audio::Segment timestamp_from/to only (the jsonb word segments are not sent).
The ayah text everywhere is Verse/Word text_uthmani in the self-hosted Noto Naskh Arabic (font-arabic), so these previews load no Quran font from the CDN.
No highlight before the first Play (the position is 0 then, which would otherwise highlight 1:1).

The AC4 SSR proof POSTs the page object with the deferred preview merged in to the SSR bundle's /render endpoint. The first response cannot carry a deferred prop, and the real bundle still renders the real props.
Previews::Recitation is named after the type; inside it the models are ::Recitation and ::Audio::Recitation.
concerns: Published transliteration 595 ('Telugu Transliteration', rc 1624) has no rows in the snapshot: its preview shows 'No text for this ayah' for every ayah rather than an explicit state.
Surah info 6 (Italian) has no ChapterInfo for surah 114, and mutashabihat has none sourced in surah 114. These show the 'No records for Surah …' empty state.
Sanitizing removes <script> elements but keeps their text content as escaped text (alert(1) is visible). It is harmless, but visible if an editor ever stored a script.

A tafsir entry whose group covers a whole surah would send that many Arabic ayahs (the text itself is capped at 20,000 characters). Recitation previews send every ayah of the surah (286 for Al-Baqarah, as text plus times), on purpose so seeking anywhere can highlight.
The browser recitation tests depend on audio-cdn.tarteel.ai being reachable, and on Chromium playing MP3.
Dark mode was not reviewed by eye. The recitation ayah card uses bg-white/text-black like the script preview.
RuboCop cannot run here. Ruby lines were kept under 120 characters by hand (checked with awk).
The 001-15 concern that the URL can keep an out-of-range value applies here too (?surah=999 shows 114).

stories.title: Home page and apps directory
stories.description: Build the home page and the apps directory from v7 on real data. Home: the hero with the shard graphic, the catalog entry points by category, real counts (resources, languages, reciters) and an apps showcase. On phones the hero text overlays the graphic so the hero stays short, as the current site does (design comment #23). Links to the wizard and other pages outside this sprint are left out or point to the catalog. Apps (`/apps`, page group `apps`): the directory with platform and resource-type filters, featured apps first, and a way to submit an app (design comment #11). App entries are data in this repo (one file plus icons) behind a serializer, so they can move to a table later without changing the page. Featured flags stay as placeholders until the maintainers supply the list.
acceptanceCriteria: With `home` on, `/` renders the Inertia home page with SSR; with it off, the old landing page. The same for `apps` and `/apps` (off gives 404, as on main). Evidence: request specs for the four states.
The three counts on the home page equal direct aggregate queries on the clone. Evidence: a spec.
At 390 px the hero's height is at most the viewport height and the heading overlaps the graphic's box. Evidence: a Playwright test with bounding boxes.
With WebGL disabled the hero shows the fallback image; with reduced motion it does not animate. Evidence: Playwright tests with the launch flag and the emulated preference.

The apps directory lists every entry in the data file; platform and resource-type filters narrow the list and are reflected in the URL; each resource-type chip links to that type page. Evidence: a Playwright test and a spec that loads and validates the data file (unique ids, known platforms and types, icon file exists).
The submit control opens the app-submission issue form. Evidence: a Playwright check of the URL and the template file in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE`.

Both pages have title, description, canonical, Open Graph and JSON-LD; home keeps the organisation and site data the old landing page emits. Evidence: request specs comparing the JSON-LD types to the old page's.
The home page's client JavaScript does not load the shard renderer before the hero is visible, and the page hydrates without warnings. Evidence: the Playwright network log and console check.
stories.notes: Prototype sources: `ds/src/app/pages/home.tsx`, `apps` page, `ds/src/app/apps-data.ts` (24 entries, icons in `ds/public/apps`), `ds/src/components/qul/shards/`. The prototype has uncommitted edits in `apps`, `home`, `chrome` and `nav`: port the working tree, it is the reviewed state. Before copying an app entry, check its `evidence` field against `../qul-redesign/research/apps-using-qul.md`; list only apps whose use of QUL is public. The old landing page uses the `devise` layout and its own shards bundle; leave both. The GitHub star count is fetched in the browser with a fallback number in the prototype; keep it out of the server render path. `LandingController` is the old controller for `/`. Issue templates are YAML issue forms now: write the app-submission form in the style of `resource_request.yml`, and check that `.github/scripts/issue-triage.js` and its test still pass with the new form present.

done: `/` with `home` on renders `site/HomePage` (Site::HomeController, Inertia, SSR); off, LandingController's old page. `/apps` with `apps` on renders `site/AppsPage` (Site::AppsController); off, 404 (no old route). Routes: a `constraints(PageGroups.constraint(:home))` block with `root to: 'site/home#show', as: :home_page` placed ABOVE the old `root to: 'landing#home'` (the new-pages block further down is too late for `/`), and an `apps` constraint block after the catalog block. Home counts come from Catalog::Stats (published resources; distinct languages, CMS row's language else content row's; published recitations; per type and category). spec/requests/site/home_spec.rb compares the props to direct SQL on both databases and checks category/type counts against `group(:resource_type).count`. Dev clone: 547 resources, 94 languages, 133 recitations.

Apps: config/apps.yml (23 entries + `showcase` order), icons in public/app-icons (16 PNGs), AppDirectory service (load, featured-first order, filters dropping unknown values), Site::AppResource/AppUseResource/AppFiltersResource/AppsIndexResource/HomeShowResource/CategoryCountResource/TypeCountResource. spec/services/app_directory_spec.rb validates the file: unique ids, known keys, platforms in AppDirectory::PLATFORMS, uses in Catalog::Taxonomy, https url/evidence, every icon exists and every icon file is referenced, showcase ids exist.

Apps page: platform and resource-type chip filters (single value each) as `?platform=&type=`, partial reload `only: ['apps','filters']`; each app's resource-type chip links to `/resources/<type>` (Inertia when `catalog` is on, plain link otherwise via NavAnchor + `catalogPages` prop). Submit links open `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/app_submission.yml` (new issue form, label `app-submission`); issue-triage test 26/26 still passes; .github/issue-triage.md table updated.

Shard ring: components/qul/shard-ring.tsx (ShardRing) with renderer.js/scene_data.js copied unchanged from app/javascript/shards (+ renderer.d.ts, ignored by Prettier). The renderer is a dynamic import started by the IntersectionObserver, a separate ~38 kB chunk; no WebGL → `/shards.webp` and no import; reduced motion → renderStill. `data-motion` = pending|running|still|fallback.

SiteNav: new `home` link (inertia when `home` is on) used by the header logo (desktop and mobile sheet), and 'Apps built with QUL' in the Contribute menu's Community aside and the footer Community column only while `apps` is on. AGENTS.md page-groups paragraph covers home and apps.

Playwright (dev, both widths): spec/browser/home.spec.ts (hydration with no console errors/warnings and counts equal props; renderer not in the HTML and not requested until a held-back IntersectionObserver report is released; canvas frames differ when animating and are identical under emulated reduced motion; at 390×844 the hero panel is ≤ 844 px tall (≈738) and the h1 box overlaps the ring box), spec/browser/home-no-webgl.spec.ts (`--disable-webgl --disable-3d-apis`: fallback image loaded, no canvas, no renderer request), spec/browser/apps.spec.ts (every id of config/apps.yml listed; filters narrow and land in the URL, the URL alone restores the view; chips link to type pages and navigate; submit href is the issue form). Full browser run: 85 passed, then the one GitHub-rate-limited test fixed and passing.

Gate: full RSpec 269/0 on the test clones (bundles rebuilt), Vitest 239 (new HomePage/AppsPage component + SSR tests, kit entries AppIcon and ShardRing), typecheck, ESLint, Prettier and `typelizer:check` clean.
decisions: The third hero count is 'recitations' (published recitation resources), not 'reciters': reciter_id is NULL on most surah recitation rows in the content DB (22 distinct ids across 133 recitations), so a reciter count would be wrong. Divergence from the AC wording, recorded here.

23 apps, not 24: the prototype working tree has 23 entries, all 'confirmed' with a public evidence link in research/apps-using-qul.md, so all were kept. `featured` stays on the four placeholders (QuranWBW, QuranCaption, quran_library, Quran Validator).

Prototype sections for pages outside the sprint are dropped (goals/wizard, starter kits, MCP/agents, the tabbed mock-data showcase, contributor ToolCards with fake progress). 'Start building' became 'Browse the library' (catalog) and 'Read the docs'. The catalog entry points are category cards listing each type with its count, linking to the type pages.
Submission is the GitHub issue form, not the prototype's in-page dialog (design comment #11 / AC). The form asks where the app credits QUL publicly, matching the directory's listing rule.
Filters are server-side like the catalog (query string, partial reload) so SSR renders the filtered view; single value per facet.

Anonymous downloads are counted on every request with no deduplication (user decision). Repeated requests and scripts raise the anonymous totals, so the popular order can be inflated; `robots.txt` and `nofollow` keep well-behaved crawlers out.

Licences have no rows. Every Licence tab says not yet confirmed.
Production runtime settings are not in this repo. Cutover needs them.
More risks are in the private sprint notes.

Editors cannot change or review the new catalog fields in the CMS this sprint (user decision). Drafted values stay unreviewed until a developer applies the data team's corrections with the task; a CMS screen is a follow-up.
decisions: RATIFIED: The new site is Inertia + React 19 + TypeScript + Vite inside this Rails app, beside the existing pages. No separate front-end app.
RATIFIED: Work lands on `qul-next`; sprint branch off it; nothing pushed until a human says go; never commit on main.
RATIFIED: Sprint files, rule doc and code live in this repo; sensitive context lives in the private sprint notes.
RATIFIED: SSR is on, proven by a spike, with client rendering as the fallback.
RATIFIED: Alba serializers define shapes once; Typelizer generates types and routes; a check fails on stale output; query objects and serializers are reusable by the public API.
RATIFIED: Fewer, deeper stories.

DEFAULT KEPT: vite_rails; `app/frontend`; own layout; Tailwind 4 for the new tree only; kit inside the front-end tree; page group setting with old views kept; RSpec request specs, Vitest, Playwright; plain links between old and new pages; no edge caching goal.

RATIFIED: The page group setting is a deploy-time environment variable read by routing constraints, not a database flag or a per-user preview switch. Why: no new dependency, no request-time lookup, switch-back is a config change. Cost: a switch needs a restart, and there is no staff-only preview in production.

PLANNER DEFAULT (shown to the user at plan time): The SSR process runs as a runit service in the same image, on localhost, with a short timeout. Why: matches how the image already runs Sidekiq; one deployable. Cost: Node shares the container's memory and CPU with Passenger.

PLANNER DEFAULT (shown to the user at plan time): Generated TypeScript types and route helpers are committed, and the drift check regenerates and diffs. Why: the image build has no database. Cost: generated files appear in diffs.

PLANNER DEFAULT (shown to the user at plan time): Page data uses Inertia props only (deferred props and partial reloads for previews and filters). The spotlight is the single JSON endpoint, internal and unversioned. Why: one data path, no client cache layer. Cost: next sprint's API serves the same data through separate controllers.

PLANNER DEFAULT (shown to the user at plan time): alba-inertia is adopted only if 001-02 proves it; otherwise page prop types are written by hand from generated serializer types and guarded by `have_exact_props` specs.

PLANNER DEFAULT (shown to the user at plan time): The catalog taxonomy (type labels and descriptions, categories, format mapping, script families, status labels) lives in one server-side file and reaches the client as props, not as a TypeScript constant. Why: the API and the pages share it. Cost: copy edits are Ruby-side.

RATIFIED (plan review): Catalog search is a query object that loads the published catalog once and normalizes, filters, counts facets and sorts in Ruby. Why: no Postgres extension is enabled, the searched text spans two databases, and facet counts become tallies. Cost: it loads every published resource per request, so it moves into SQL behind the same interface if the catalog grows into the thousands.

RATIFIED (plan review): `recommended` is a boolean flag separate from the lifecycle status (stable, beta, legacy, superseded). Why: endorsement is not a lifecycle stage, and a status filter of stable must keep the recommended resources. Cost: one more column and one more drafted field.

PLANNER DEFAULT (shown to the user at plan time): New catalog fields are plain columns on `downloadable_resources` (status, superseded-by, recommended, script_family, rendering, display_name, review column as JSON) and a relation type column on the link table; drafted links are recorded in the source resource's review column. Display names are stored, not computed per request.
PLANNER DEFAULT (shown to the user at plan time): Migrations in this sprint add no constraint a production row could violate before backfill; tightening constraints is a cutover step.

RATIFIED: No CMS form changes this sprint. Corrections and review marks go through a task; changing a drafted field outside a backfill counts as reviewing it. Why: keeps the CMS untouched for now. Cost: only a developer can apply corrections.
PLANNER DEFAULT (shown to the user at plan time): The new download URL has no file token and is built from the resource slug and the file; the old token URL keeps working under the same rules.

RATIFIED (plan review, replaces the cookie-per-day deduplication): Anonymous downloads add 1 to an anonymous counter column on the file with an atomic update. No cookie, no visitor id, and the request's address is never used. The column is separate so the signed-in recount cannot erase it. Why: nothing about a visitor is stored, no table to purge, and it matches signed-in counting, which is not deduplicated either. Cost: repeated requests and scripts count every time.
PLANNER DEFAULT (shown to the user at plan time): After sign-in for a download, the user returns to the resource page and the download starts there, instead of returning straight to the file URL.

PLANNER DEFAULT (shown to the user at plan time): Preview data is one deferred `preview` prop per detail page, keyed by page or surah in the query string, behind one server-side preview interface with a provider per kind.
PLANNER DEFAULT (shown to the user at plan time): Detail tabs are client-side with the tab in the query string; only the preview is deferred.
